build_system: Node.js with 'npm run dev' (nodemon server.js) for backend. Android: Gradle via './gradlew assembleDebug' from 'hookaDrop App/HookahDrop/'.
test_framework: No automated test suite present. Verification is manual: curl for backend, app build + device/emulator run for Android.
build_command: npm run dev  (backend) | .\gradlew assembleDebug  (Android, from 'hookaDrop App\HookahDrop\')
test_command: Manual curl test for backend. Android: .\gradlew assembleDebug then install on device/emulator.
verification_instructions: Backend: start with 'npm run dev', get JWT via POST /api/auth/login, then POST /api/support with Authorization header. Android: run .\gradlew assembleDebug, install APK, fill Help & Support form, tap Submit.
environment_constraints: server.js uses ES modules ('type: module' in package.json) — all new .js files must use import/export syntax, not require(). EMAIL_PASSWORD in .env must be a Gmail App Password, not the regular Gmail password.
contribution_requirements: Follow existing ES module pattern. No new npm dependencies needed (nodemailer already installed). New route files must follow the import-router-export-default pattern. Controller functions must be named exports.
key_patterns: Routes: import protectRoute from '../middleware/protectRoute.js'; router.post('/', protectRoute, handler); export default router. Controllers: named async export function handler(req, res). Email: import { mailSender } from '../controller/mailerSender.js'; await mailSender(toAddress, subject, htmlString). Android HTTP calls: lifecycleScope.launch { val resp = ApiClient.post('/api/path', JSONObject(...), session.getJwtToken()); if (resp.isSuccess) { ... } else { toast(resp.userFriendlyError()) } }.
directory_structure: e-commerce-backend-main/ — root of Node.js backend. controller/ — business logic (mailerSender.js is key). routes/ — Express routers, one file per domain. middleware/ — protectRoute.js, requireRole.js. hookaDrop App/HookahDrop/ — Android project root. app/src/main/java/com/hookahdrop/app/ — Kotlin source. network/ — ApiClient.kt (HTTP) and ApiModels.kt (JSON mapping). data/ — SessionManager.kt (auth token, user info). app/src/main/res/layout/ — XML layouts including activity_help_support.xml.
